page: Amazon Web Services c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 64-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor operating at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Delivered through the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring each vCPU has exclusive hardware execution resources. Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB of DDR5 RAM clocked at 5 GHz, producing a compute-oriented 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes no local disk storage, relying on external network volumes, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are installed.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional multi-core performance, positioning the instance in the top tier of compute systems. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 22073.0, a PassMark CPU score of 93359.17, and a stress-ng multi-core measurement of 196253.01. Processor extensions including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16), AES, and SHA-NI assist high-throughput execution, demonstrated by a Clang software compilation score of 72495.0 and ray tracing performance of 97810.0. Memory throughput remains robust, delivering 296.16 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and 150.74 GB/sec in write tests.

By pairing dedicated physical AMD cores with a dense 2.0 GB per-core DDR5 configuration and excluding local disks, the instance provides high compute density without incurring costs for unneeded storage or oversized memory allocations. This hardware profile suits compute-bound workloads, such as parallel software compilation, CPU-based machine learning inference, scientific simulations, financial modeling, and high-concurrency web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The system incorporates 128.0 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 5 GHz, delivering a dedicated 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU without simultaneous multithreading. It provides a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps, includes no local storage, and contains no graphics processing units. In empirical benchmarks, the platform demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing power, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 22073.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 93359.17 alongside strong AVX-512 vector support. The absence of bundled disks and moderate memory footprint make it a resource-efficient choice for compute-dominated environments, such as large-scale software compilation, CPU-driven machine learning inference, distributed batch processing, and high-traffic web applications.
